images.author: CDC / Dr. Frederick Murphy
images.why: Best match for the characteristic shepherd’s-crook silhouette. CDC’s caption identifies an electron micrograph of the 1976 Ebola isolate, showing its distinctive 6-shape, nucleocapsid and envelope projections. Colourised purple background.

images.author: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
images.why: Caption confirms colourised SEM of red filamentous Ebola particles attached to and budding from a blue VERO E6 cell at 25,000×. Strong contrasting colours and numerous filaments offer flexible 9:10 cropping.

images.author: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
images.why: Scientific caption specifically identifies SEM of Ebola virus Makona from the West African epidemic, coloured red on blue Vero cells. Strong colour separation; the generic page title incorrectly describes a blood cell, but the scientific caption confirms Ebola.

images.author: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
images.why: Caption identifies SEM of green Ebola particles budding from and attached to orange infected VERO E6 cells. Actual microscopy colourised in Halloween colours, with a dense field suitable for a full-bleed crop.

images.author: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
images.why: Caption confirms colourised SEM of filamentous Ebola particles budding from a chronically infected VERO E6 cell at 35,000×, captured and colour-enhanced at NIAID’s Integrated Research Facility.

images.author: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
images.why: Caption confirms SEM of filamentous Ebola particles budding from an infected VERO E6 cell. Vivid red-and-yellow Halloween colourisation of real microscopy provides an alternative dramatic palette.
